m.1.1: Śaunaka said: O Sūta, O greatly wise one, knower of all doctrines, O lord, tell me the essence of the sacred stories, especially of the Purāṇas. ॥1॥
m.1.2: How do good conduct, true devotion and discernment grow? And how do good people bring about the removal of their own inner distortions? ॥2॥
m.1.3: Here in the terrible Kali age beings have mostly fallen into a demonic nature. What indeed is the supreme means for purifying that condition? ॥3॥
m.1.4: Now tell me that means which is the supreme reality, the highest good among goods, and the purifier of purifiers. ॥4॥
m.1.5: That means by which the self is quickly and especially purified, and by which, dear one, the attainment of Śiva may come to one whose mind is ever pure. ॥5॥
m.1.6: Sūta said: Blessed are you, O tiger among sages, eager with love for hearing. Therefore, having reflected with a clear mind, I shall tell you the most excellent scripture. ॥6॥
m.1.7: Hear, child, this divine elixir, perfected through all doctrines, which increases devotion and the like and brings delight to Śiva. ॥7॥
m.1.8: This excellent, supreme Śaiva Purāṇa, which destroys the great terror of the serpent of Time, was spoken by Śiva long ago, O sage. ॥8॥
m.1.9: Following the instruction of the sage Sanatkumāra, it was narrated by Vyāsa in abridged form with great reverence, for the welfare of those born in the Kali age. ॥9॥
m.1.10: Other than this Śaiva Purāṇa, O sage, there is nothing for the purification of the mind, especially for those born in the Kali age. ॥10॥
m.1.11: That wise man who has great merit from a former birth — in that greatly fortunate one, O sage, love for this Purāṇa arises. ॥11॥
m.1.12: This Śiva Purāṇa is indeed the supreme, excellent scripture; it should be known as the very form of Śiva on earth and be honoured in every way. ॥12॥
m.1.13: By reading and hearing it, the devoted best of men at once obtains the attainment of Śiva's abode, since it is the means of all attainments. ॥13॥
m.1.14: Therefore its reading is to be sought by men with every effort; likewise, hearing it with love grants the fruit of all desires. ॥14॥
m.1.15: By hearing the Purāṇa of Śambhu a man becomes sinless; having enjoyed abundant pleasures, he reaches the world of Śiva. ॥15॥
m.1.16: Whatever merit comes from the Rājasūya and from a hundred Agniṣṭoma sacrifices, that merit one obtains merely by hearing the story of Śambhu. ॥16॥
m.1.17: Those who hear, O sage, the Śaiva Purāṇa, the excellent scripture, should not be regarded as mere men; they are Rudras themselves, without doubt. ॥17॥
m.1.18: The sages know that the dust of the lotus-feet of those who hear that Purāṇa and likewise recite it is itself equal to the holy places. ॥18॥
m.1.19: Embodied beings who wish to reach the state of final beatitude should always hear the spotless Śaiva Purāṇa with devotion. ॥19॥
m.1.20: If he is unable to hear it continually, O best of sages, then with a restrained mind he should hear it daily for at least a muhūrta. ॥20॥
m.1.21: If a man is unable to hear it every day, O sage, he should hear the Śiva Purāṇa during the holy months and the like. ॥21॥
m.1.22: Those who hear that Purāṇa for a muhūrta, or half of that, or half of that again, or even a moment — for them there will be no evil destiny. ॥22॥
m.1.23: O lord of sages, the man who listens to that Purāṇa crosses over worldly existence, having burnt down the great forest of karma. ॥23॥
m.1.24: Whatever merit lies in all gifts or in all sacrifices, O sage, that fruit becomes firmly secured through hearing the Purāṇa of Śambhu. ॥24॥
m.1.25: Especially in the Kali age, O sage, apart from hearing the Śaiva Purāṇa there is indeed no higher dharma for men that brings about the means of liberation. ॥25॥
m.1.26: Hearing the Purāṇa of Śambhu and likewise chanting his name are truly the fruit of the wish-granting tree for men, without doubt. ॥26॥
m.1.27: In the Kali age, for the welfare of dull-witted men whose hearts have abandoned dharma and right conduct, Śambhu created the nectar-essence called the Purāṇa. ॥27॥
m.1.28: By drinking nectar, a man would himself alone become free from age and death; but the nectar of Śambhu's story makes the whole family free from age and death. ॥28॥
m.1.29: Always to be cherished, always to be cherished, always and especially to be cherished is this supremely purifying story of the Śiva Purāṇa. ॥29॥
m.1.30: What shall I say of the fruit of merely hearing the story of this Śiva Purāṇa? Śiva himself comes to dwell in the hearer's mind. ॥30॥
m.1.31: This text of twenty-four thousand verses, in seven saṃhitās, is fully complete with the threefold devotion; one should hear it with great reverence. ॥31॥
m.1.32: The Vidyeśvara Saṃhitā is the first, the second is the Rudra Saṃhitā, the third is called Śatarudra, and the fourth is Koṭirudra. ॥32॥
m.1.33: The fifth is declared to be the Umā Saṃhitā, the sixth the Kailāsa Saṃhitā, the seventh is called Vāyavīya; thus there are seven saṃhitās here. ॥33॥
m.1.34: The divine Purāṇa named after Śiva, with its seven saṃhitās, stands supreme, equal to Brahman, granting the goal that is above all. ॥34॥
m.1.35: Whoever reads with reverence this Śiva Purāṇa in its entirety, with its seven saṃhitās, is called one liberated while living. ॥35॥
m.1.36: A man wanders through ignorance in this worldly existence, O sage, only so long as the excellent Śaiva Purāṇa has not reached his ears. ॥36॥
m.1.37: What use are many scriptures heard, and Purāṇas that bring confusion? The Śaiva Purāṇa alone roars triumphantly by its gift of liberation. ॥37॥
m.1.38: In whatever house the story of this Śiva Purāṇa takes place, that house becomes a holy place, destroying the sins of those who dwell there. ॥38॥
m.1.39: Thousands of Aśvamedha sacrifices and hundreds of Vājapeyas are surely not worth even a sixteenth part of the Śiva Purāṇa. ॥39॥
m.1.40: So long is he called a sinner, a doer of sin, O best of sages, as long as he does not hear the Śiva Purāṇa with true devotion. ॥40॥
m.1.41: The Gaṅgā and the other holy rivers, the seven sacred cities, and Gayā likewise — nowhere do they attain equality with this Śiva Purāṇa. ॥41॥
m.1.42: If one desires the supreme goal, one should daily recite with one's own mouth, with devotion, a verse of the Śiva Purāṇa, or even half a verse. ॥42॥
m.1.43: Whoever constantly expounds this Śiva Purāṇa with its meaning, or reads it daily with love, is a meritorious soul; there is no doubt. ॥43॥
m.1.44: Indeed, the wise one who listens to this with devotion at the time of death — to him the great Lord, fully pleased, grants his own abode. ॥44॥
m.1.45: Whoever worships this Śiva Purāṇa daily with reverence, having enjoyed all desires here, at the end attains the abode of Śiva. ॥45॥
m.1.46: He who, unwearied, daily honours this Śiva Purāṇa properly with silk cloths and the like is always happy. ॥46॥
m.1.47: The pure Śaiva Purāṇa, the whole treasure of the Śaivas, should be served with reverence and effort by one who seeks happiness hereafter and here. ॥47॥
m.1.48: The supreme, pure Śaiva Purāṇa, bestower of the four aims of life, should always be heard with love, and especially be read. ॥48॥
m.1.49: Among the Vedas, histories and treatises, the Śaiva Purāṇa should by all means be known by seekers of liberation as supreme, great and conducive to the highest good. ॥49॥
m.1.50: This Śaiva Purāṇa, foremost for the knowers of the Self, the supreme reality, should always be served and worshipped by the good; it allays the three afflictions, ever gives happiness, and is dear as life to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Īśa and the other gods. ॥50॥
m.1.51: I, with a serene mind, always bow to the Śiva Purāṇa. May Śiva be pleased and grant me love for his feet. ॥51॥
m.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The glory of the Śivapurāṇa, in the Śivapurāṇa Māhātmya of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
m.2.1: Śaunaka said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you are blessed, a knower of the highest truth. Out of kindness you have indeed narrated to us this wondrous, divine story. ॥1॥
m.2.2: This wondrous story we have heard destroys the flood of sins, brings about purity of mind, and gives rise to Śiva's satisfaction. ॥2॥
m.2.3: There is nothing on earth equal to this story, nothing higher than the highest — this we have come to know with certainty through your kindness. ॥3॥
m.2.4: Which sinners in the Kali age are purified by this story? Kindly tell us of them, O Sūta, and make the world fulfilled. ॥4॥
m.2.5: Sūta said: Those men who commit sins, who delight in wicked conduct, who are villainous and ever given to lust and the like — even they are surely purified by this. ॥5॥
m.2.6: This is indeed the supreme sacrifice of knowledge, always granting worldly enjoyment and liberation, the purifier of all sins and the cause of Śiva's satisfaction. ॥6॥
m.2.7: Those who are tormented by craving, devoid of truth, who revile their father and mother, who are hypocritical and violent — even they are surely purified by this. ॥7॥
m.2.8: Those who have abandoned the duties of their own caste and stage of life, and who are full of envy — they are purified by this sacrifice of knowledge, even in the Kali age. ॥8॥
m.2.9: Those who practise fraud and deceit, and those who are cruel and utterly merciless — they are purified by this sacrifice of knowledge, even in the Kali age. ॥9॥
m.2.10: Those who constantly fatten themselves on the property of brāhmaṇas, and those who delight in adultery — they are purified by this sacrifice of knowledge, even in the Kali age. ॥10॥
m.2.11: Those who are ever devoted to sin, and those who are crooked and evil-minded — they are purified by this sacrifice of knowledge, even in the Kali age. ॥11॥
m.2.12: The impure, the evil-witted, the restless, those who consume what belongs to the gods — they are purified by this sacrifice of knowledge, even in the Kali age. ॥12॥
m.2.13: The merit of this Purāṇa is excellent, destroying even the great sins; it grants enjoyment and liberation and is the cause of Śiva's satisfaction. ॥13॥
m.2.14: In this very connection they cite this ancient legend, by merely hearing which the destruction of sin fully comes about. ॥14॥
m.2.15: In the city of the Kirātas there lived a brāhmaṇa weak in knowledge, poor, a seller of juices, who had turned his back on Vedic dharma. ॥15॥
m.2.16: He had abandoned the twilight rites and bathing, was intent on the livelihood of a vaiśya, was known as Devarāja, and cheated people who trusted him. ॥16॥
m.2.17: He killed brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras and others too, under various pretexts, and carried off their respective wealth. ॥17॥
m.2.18: Afterwards he amassed great riches through unrighteousness, but not even a little of that sinner's wealth here went to dharma. ॥18॥
m.2.19: Once that brāhmaṇa went to a certain pond to bathe; there, seeing a courtesan named Śobhāvatī, he became utterly agitated. ॥19॥
m.2.20: Then the beautiful woman, delighted on knowing the wealthy brāhmaṇa to be under her sway, so charmed him by her conversation that his mind became full of affection. ॥20॥
m.2.21: He resolved to make her his woman, and she likewise to make him her husband; thus, both overcome by desire, they sported together for a long time. ॥21॥
m.2.22: In sitting, lying, drinking, eating and playing, the two always behaved toward each other like husband and wife. ॥22॥
m.2.23: Though restrained again and again by his mother, father and wife, he, intent on sinful ways, did not heed their words. ॥23॥
m.2.24: One night, overcome by jealousy, the wicked man killed his mother, father and wife as they slept, and likewise took their wealth. ॥24॥
m.2.25: His own wealth, and likewise the wealth of his father and the others — all of it the lustful man, his mind fixed on her, gave to the courtesan. ॥25॥
m.2.26: That sinner, an eater of forbidden food, greedy for drinking liquor, the lowest of brāhmaṇas, always ate from a single plate together with the courtesan. ॥26॥
m.2.27: Once, by the turn of fate, he came to Pratiṣṭhāna; there he saw a temple of Śiva surrounded by holy people. ॥27॥
m.2.28: Staying there, that brāhmaṇa, severely afflicted by fever, continually heard the story of Śiva issuing from the mouth of a brāhmaṇa. ॥28॥
m.2.29: At the end of a month Devarāja, afflicted by fever, died; bound with nooses by Yama's servants, he was dragged by force to Yama's city. ॥29॥
m.2.30: Meanwhile Śiva's attendants, radiant white, their hands adorned with tridents, all their limbs shining with ash, their bodies adorned with rudrākṣa beads — ॥30॥
m.2.31: — coming from Śiva's world, went in anger to Yama's city, and striking his messengers and threatening them again and again, ॥31॥
m.2.32: having freed Devarāja and seated him in a most wondrous aerial chariot, when the messengers were eager to go to Kailāsa, ॥32॥
m.2.33: then a great uproar arose in the midst of Yama's city. Hearing it, Dharmarāja came out of his palace. ॥33॥
m.2.34: Then, seeing the four messengers, like other Rudras in person, Dharmarāja, knower of dharma, worshipped them according to rule. ॥34॥
m.2.35: Through the eye of knowledge Yama understood the whole affair; out of fear he asked nothing of the messengers of the great-souled Śambhu. ॥35॥
m.2.36: Worshipped and entreated, they then went to Kailāsa and handed him over to Śiva, together with Ambā, that ocean of compassion. ॥36॥
m.2.37: Blessed is the story of the Śiva Purāṇa, supremely purifying, by merely hearing which even a great sinner becomes a sharer in liberation. ॥37॥
m.2.38: He reached the great abode of Sadāśiva, the supreme realm, the highest state, which the knowers of the Veda declare to be situated above all worlds. ॥38॥
m.2.39: Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras and other living beings too — many were harmed out of greed for wealth by that sinner; ॥39॥
m.2.40: yet the twice-born Devarāja, slayer of his mother, father and wife, frequenter of a courtesan and drinker of liquor, went there and was liberated in an instant. ॥40॥
m.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The liberation of Devarāja, in the Śivapurāṇa Māhātmya of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
m.3.1: Śaunaka said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you are all-knowing, O great-minded one. By your grace I am fulfilled; I am fulfilled again and again. ॥1॥
m.3.2: Having heard this story, my mind rejoices greatly. Tell me another story of Śambhu too, one that increases love for him. ॥2॥
m.3.3: In the world, liberation is nowhere found for those who drink nectar; but the drinking of the nectar of Śambhu's story directly bestows liberation. ॥3॥
m.3.4: Blessed, blessed is the story of Śambhu, and you too are blessed, truly blessed, by the mere hearing of which a man would go to Śiva's world. ॥4॥
m.3.5: Sūta said: Listen, O Śaunaka; I shall tell before you even what is secret, since you are the foremost of Śiva's devotees and the best of knowers of the Veda. ॥5॥
m.3.6: In a region near the sea there is a village called Bāṣkala, where live most sinful people who have abandoned the dharma of the Veda. ॥6॥
m.3.7: They are wicked, their minds set on base objects, godless, crooked in conduct, farmers bearing weapons, enjoyers of others' wives, villains. ॥7॥
m.3.8: They know nothing at all of knowledge, dispassion, and true dharma; with beast-like minds, they are devoted to gatherings rich in the hearing of vile talk. ॥8॥
m.3.9: The other classes too are ill-minded villains averse to their own dharma; they are ever engaged in evil deeds and always given to sensual objects. ॥9॥
m.3.10: And all the women are crooked, wanton, lusting after sin, ill-minded, unchaste, and devoid of good conduct and practice. ॥10॥
m.3.11: Thus, in that village called Bāṣkala, the dwelling of wicked people, there lived a certain brāhmaṇa named Binduga, a great villain. ॥11॥
m.3.12: That evil-souled great sinner, though he had a good wife, went the wrong way; with his mind overwhelmed by lust, he became the keeper of a prostitute. ॥12॥
m.3.13: Abandoning his own wife, named Cañculā, who was always virtuous, that wicked man, tormented by the arrows of Smara, sported with the prostitute. ॥13॥
m.3.14: Thus a long time passed for that evildoer. And Cañculā, though tormented by desire, held back in distress out of fear of violating her own dharma. ॥14॥
m.3.15: Then his wife too, her fresh youth in full bloom, unable to bear the onset of desire, turned away from her own dharma. ॥15॥
m.3.16: Joined with a sinful paramour at night, she secretly enjoyed him, deceiving her husband's sight—she, her virtue lost, going on the wrong path. ॥16॥
m.3.17: Once, O sage, he saw his own wife Cañculā, of evil conduct, overcome by desire, together with her paramour at night. ॥17॥
m.3.18: Seeing his defiled wife, her mind attached to evil deeds, together with her paramour at night, he rushed forward swiftly in anger. ॥18॥
m.3.19: Realising that the wicked Binduga had come into the house, that villainous, deceitful paramour fled quickly and in haste. ॥19॥
m.3.20: Then that Binduga, most evil-minded, seized his wife, threatened her, and beat her again and again with his clenched fist. ॥20॥
m.3.21: That woman Cañculā, wanton and wicked, beaten by her husband, grew angry and fearlessly spoke to her wicked husband Binduga. ॥21॥
m.3.22: Cañculā said: You, foolish-minded, sport at will every day with a prostitute, abandoning me, your own wife, young and devoted to serving her husband. ॥22॥
m.3.23: For me, a beautiful young woman whose mind is overwhelmed by desire, what recourse would there be without enjoyment with a husband? Tell me. ॥23॥
m.3.24: I am very beautiful and overwhelmed by fresh youth; how can I, with afflicted mind, bear the pain of desire without union with you? ॥24॥
m.3.25: Sūta said: Thus addressed by her, that fool Binduga, the dull-witted, base brāhmaṇa, sinful, averse to his own dharma, wicked, replied. ॥25॥
m.3.26: Binduga said: What you have said, with your mind agitated by desire, is indeed true. Therefore I shall tell you what is beneficial; listen, beloved, and cast off fear. ॥26॥
m.3.27: Always sport with paramours, with a fearless mind; giving them the highest pleasure, draw wealth from them. ॥27॥
m.3.28: Give all that wealth to me, whose mind is attached to the prostitute; surely there would be great gain for you as well as for me. ॥28॥
m.3.29: Sūta said: Hearing these words of her husband, Cañculā, his wife, delighted at heart, accepted her husband's words and said, so be it. ॥29॥
m.3.30: Having made such an agreement, that couple of wicked minds became devoted to evil deeds, with fearless, depraved hearts. ॥30॥
m.3.31: Thus a long time passed fruitlessly for that couple, engaged in evil conduct and deluded in mind. ॥31॥
m.3.32: Then that ill-minded brāhmaṇa Binduga, husband of a fallen woman, met his death in time, and the villain went to hell. ॥32॥
m.3.33: Having suffered the torments of hell for many days, that dull-witted sinner became a terrifying piśāca on the Vindhya mountain. ॥33॥
m.3.34: When that husband of evil conduct, Binduga, had died, she, utterly deluded, lived for a long time in her own house with her sons. ॥34॥
m.3.35: Thus sporting with paramours, that woman named Cañculā remained delighted and given to lust, her youth somewhat passed. ॥35॥
m.3.36: Once, by the turn of fate, when a holy festival had arrived, that woman came with her relatives to the sacred place Gokarṇa. ॥36॥
m.3.37: Then, as it happened, she went and bathed casually in the waters of some holy ford, and wandered here and there with her relatives. ॥37॥
m.3.38: Then, in a certain temple, she heard from the mouth of a learned man an auspicious, holy, Purāṇic tale of Śambhu. ॥38॥
m.3.39: In hell, Yama's servants thrust a red-hot iron bar into the private parts of women attached to paramours. ॥39॥
m.3.40: Hearing this story, told by the Purāṇa-reciter, which increases dispassion, she became agitated with fear and trembled there. ॥40॥
m.3.41: When the story was over and the people had gone away, that woman, frightened, spoke in private to that Śaiva Brāhmaṇa, the reciter. ॥41॥
m.3.42: Cañculā said: O Brāhmaṇa, hear my wicked conduct, committed by me who did not know my own dharma. Having heard it, O master, lift me up, showing even boundless compassion. ॥42॥
m.3.43: O lord, very grave sin has been committed by me, dull-witted as I was; blinded by lust, I spent my whole youth in harlotry. ॥43॥
m.3.44: Having heard today these words of yours, swelling with the flavour of dispassion, I have become greatly afraid, trembling, and have taken to renunciation. ॥44॥
m.3.45: Shame on me, dull-witted and sinful, my mind deluded by desire, blameworthy, attached to evil objects of sense, and turned away from my own dharma! ॥45॥
m.3.46: For the sake of a little pleasure, I, in ignorance, committed a terrible great sin, destructive of my own true good and causing extreme suffering. ॥46॥
m.3.47: What dreadful, pain-giving evil destinies, alas, shall I go to! What wise one will come to me there, whose mind delighted in the wrong path? ॥47॥
m.3.48: At death, how shall I look upon those terrifying messengers of Yama? How shall I keep my composure while being forcibly bound with nooses at the throat? ॥48॥
m.3.49: How shall I endure in hell the cutting of my body into pieces, and the great torment there, especially painful? ॥49॥
m.3.50: By day, grieving, how shall I carry on the activity of my senses? At night, overwhelmed with sorrow, how shall I get sleep? ॥50॥
m.3.51: Alas, I am struck down, I am burnt, my heart is torn apart; I am utterly ruined, utterly a sinner am I. ॥51॥
m.3.52: Alas, O Fate! You forcibly gave me, a great sinner, an evil mind, by which one departs from one's own dharma, the bringer of all happiness—alas! ॥52॥
m.3.53: O Brāhmaṇa, whatever dreadful pain an embodied being suffers when impaled on a stake or falling from a lofty mountain peak, mine is ten million times greater than that. ॥53॥
m.3.54: Even by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices or bathing in the Gaṅgā for a hundred years, there would hardly arise purification of my very grievous sin. ॥54॥
m.3.55: What shall I do? Where shall I go? To whom shall I resort for refuge? Who in this world will save me as I fall into the ocean of hell? ॥55॥
m.3.56: You alone are my guru, O Brāhmaṇa; you are my mother and you are my father. Lift me up, lift me up, wretched as I am, who have come to you alone for refuge. ॥56॥
m.3.57: Sūta said: Thus, she, in whom disgust with worldly life had arisen, fell at his two feet; the wise Brāhmaṇa compassionately raised her up and spoke. ॥57॥
m.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The dispassion of Cañculā, in the Śivapurāṇa Māhātmya of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
m.4.1: The brahmin said: Fortunately, by Śiva's grace, you have awakened in time, having heard this excellent story of the Śiva Purāṇa, which is full of dispassion. ॥1॥
m.4.2: Do not be afraid, O wife of a brāhmaṇa; go to Śiva for refuge. Through Śiva's grace all sin is destroyed at once. ॥2॥
m.4.3: I shall tell you the supreme thing, filled with Śiva's glory, by which you will always have a destiny that brings happiness. ॥3॥
m.4.4: From merely hearing the holy story such a mind has arisen in you—pure, filled with remorse, and with dispassion towards sense-objects. ॥4॥
m.4.5: For sinners, remorse is the supreme atonement for sins; the good have described it as the cleanser of all sins for everyone. ॥5॥
m.4.6: Purity comes through remorse alone; the repentant one performs the expiation as taught by the good, which indeed cleanses all sins. ॥6॥
m.4.7: A man who undertakes expiation according to rule but without fear of his sin generally does not attain a good destiny; the remorseful one does, without doubt. ॥7॥
m.4.8: Purification of the mind arises from hearing the story of this Śiva Purāṇa as by no other means. ॥8॥
m.4.9: Just as a mirror being cleaned becomes spotless, so the mind attains purity through this story, without doubt. ॥9॥
m.4.10: In the purified mind of men Śiva abides together with Ambikā; then the pure-souled one goes to the supreme abode of Śambhu with Ambā. ॥10॥
m.4.11: Therefore this story is held to be the means for all classes of beings; for this purpose Mahādeva earnestly composed it. ॥11॥
m.4.12: Through this story meditation on Girijā's Lord is perfected; from meditation comes supreme knowledge, and from that, liberation (kaivalya) certainly follows. ॥12॥
m.4.13: He who has not perfected meditation on Śaṅkara but merely listens to the story attains meditation on Śambhu in another birth and reaches the supreme goal. ॥13॥
m.4.14: By hearing this story and meditating on Umā's Lord, many remorseful sinners have attained perfection. ॥14॥
m.4.15: For men, hearing the holy story is the seed of all good; it should be duly cultivated according to the proper way, as it removes the disease of worldly bondage. ॥15॥
m.4.16: By hearing Śambhu's story, then by reflecting on it in the heart, and by deep contemplation, purity of mind arises fully. ॥16॥
m.4.17: Hence devotion to Maheśa arises surely, together with her two sons, knowledge and dispassion; by his grace, divine liberation follows from that, without doubt. ॥17॥
m.4.18: One devoid of it should be known as a beast (paśu), his mind attached to the bonds of Māyā; he certainly is never freed from the bondage of saṃsāra. ॥18॥
m.4.19: Therefore, O brāhmaṇa's wife, with your mind turned away from sense-objects, listen with devotion to this supremely purifying story of Śambhu. ॥19॥
m.4.20: As you listen to this holy story of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self, your mind will attain purity, and then you will obtain liberation. ॥20॥
m.4.21: For one who meditates on Śiva's lotus-feet with a pure mind, liberation comes in a single birth—I speak the truth, the truth. ॥21॥
m.4.22: Sūta said: Having said this, that best of brāhmaṇas, an eminent Śaiva whose mind was moist with compassion, pure in soul and devoted to meditation on Śiva, fell silent. ॥22॥
m.4.23: Then that wife of Binduga, named Cañculā, addressed thus by that brāhmaṇa, became serene in mind, her eyes filled with tears. ॥23॥
m.4.24: Joyful at heart, Cañculā quickly fell at the feet of that lord of brāhmaṇas, and with folded hands she said, I am fulfilled. ॥24॥
m.4.25: Then she rose, anxious, with folded hands, and that wise woman, endowed with dispassion, spoke in a choked voice to that great Śaiva brāhmaṇa. ॥25॥
m.4.26: Cañculā said: O brāhmaṇa, best of Śaivas, master, blessed are you, a seer of the highest truth, devoted to helping others, worthy of praise among the truly good! ॥26॥
m.4.27: Save me, save me, O holy one, who am falling into the ocean of hell—I who, having heard this beautiful Śaiva story unfolded with the meaning of the Purāṇa, ॥27॥
m.4.28: I have become detached in mind from sense-objects on every side, and now I have great and firm faith in hearing this Purāṇa. ॥28॥
m.4.29: Sūta said: Having said this with folded hands and received his grace, she remained there, eager to hear that Purāṇa, devoted to serving him. ॥29॥
m.4.30: Then the wise brāhmaṇa, best of Śaivas, in that very place made that woman hear the holy story of that Purāṇa. ॥30॥
m.4.31: Thus in that great holy place, from that very best of brāhmaṇas, she heard the most excellent story of the Śiva Purāṇa, ॥31॥
m.4.32: which increases devotion, knowledge and dispassion and bestows liberation; having heard that supreme holy story, she became truly fulfilled. ॥32॥
m.4.33: By the compassion of that true guru her mind was quickly purified, and by Śiva's grace she attained meditation on Śambhu's form. ॥33॥
m.4.34: Thus, relying on the true guru and having gained a right understanding of Śiva, she meditated again and again on Śambhu's body made of consciousness and bliss. ॥34॥
m.4.35: Bathing daily in the water of the holy ford, wearing matted hair and bark garments, her whole body smeared with ash, adorned with rudrākṣa beads, ॥35॥
m.4.36: absorbed in repeating Śiva's name, restrained in speech, eating sparingly, she pleased Śiva by the path taught by her guru. ॥36॥
m.4.37: In this way, O Śaunaka, a long time passed for that Cañculā as she practised supreme meditation on Śambhu right there. ॥37॥
m.4.38: Then, when her time was complete, Cañculā, endowed with the triad of devotion, knowledge and dispassion, gave up her body without effort. ॥38॥
m.4.39: There came swiftly a divine aerial chariot sent by the Enemy of Tripura, accompanied by his own attendants and endowed with manifold splendour. ॥39॥
m.4.40: Then, having mounted it, she, with all her impurities destroyed, was immediately led to Śiva's city by Maheśa's excellent attendants. ॥40॥
m.4.41: Bearing a divine form, herself divine, endowed with divine limbs, crowned with the half-moon, fair-complexioned, and adorned with shining divine ornaments, ॥41॥
m.4.42: having gone there, she saw the three-eyed Mahādeva, the eternal one, being served by the gods Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others, ॥42॥
m.4.43: being worshipped with true devotion by Gaṇeśa, Bhṛṅgī, Nandīśa, Vīrabhadreśvara and others, radiant like ten million suns, ॥43॥
m.4.44: blue-throated, five-faced, three-eyed, moon-crested, bearing on his left side Gaurī, radiant like a mass of lightning, ॥44॥
m.4.45: white as camphor, lord of Gaurī, wearing all ornaments, his body gleaming with white ash, clad in white garments, intensely brilliant. ॥45॥
m.4.46: Seeing Śaṅkara thus, that woman Cañculā rejoiced exceedingly; greatly delighted, in eager haste she bowed again and again. ॥46॥
m.4.47: With joined palms, joyful, loving, contented and humble, she was filled with tears of bliss and thrilled with horripilation. ॥47॥
m.4.48: Then, out of compassion, Pārvatī and Śaṅkara brought her close to them and looked upon her with a gracious glance. ॥48॥
m.4.49: Lovingly Pārvatī made her, now divine in form, her own companion; and there Cañculā, beloved of Binduga, was endowed with divine happiness. ॥49॥
m.4.50: In that eternal world, which is a dense light of supreme bliss, having obtained an unshakable abode, she attained unbroken happiness. ॥50॥
m.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The attainment of a good end by Cañculā, in the Śivapurāṇa Māhātmya of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
m.5.1: Śaunaka said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, blessed are you, whose mind is devoted to Śiva! You have made us hear this wondrous story, which increases devotion. ॥1॥
m.5.2: Having gone there, what did Cañculā, who had attained the good destination, do? Tell that in detail, O wise one, and also what became of her husband. ॥2॥
m.5.3: Sūta said: Once she approached the goddess Umā, bowed to her, and, with joined hands, overflowing with supreme bliss, praised her well. ॥3॥
m.5.4: Cañculā said: O Girijā, mother of Skanda, you are served by men at all times. O giver of all happiness, beloved of Śambhu, you whose form is Brahman. ॥4॥
m.5.5: You are to be served by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and others; you are with attributes and also without attributes. You are the primal, subtle Prakṛti, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss. ॥5॥
m.5.6: You bring about creation, preservation and dissolution; you possess the three guṇas and are the abode of the three gods; you are the supreme one who firmly establishes Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa. ॥6॥
m.5.7: Sūta said: Having thus praised that great goddess, Cañculā, who had attained the good destination, fell silent, her shoulders bowed and her eyes full of tears of love. ॥7॥
m.5.8: Then Pārvatī, beloved of Śaṅkara, affectionate to her devotees, filled with compassion, spoke with great affection to that Cañculā. ॥8॥
m.5.9: Pārvatī said: O Cañculā, my friend, O beautiful one, I am well pleased by this hymn. What boon do you ask? Speak; there is nothing that cannot be given to you. ॥9॥
m.5.10: Sūta said: Thus addressed by Girijā, Cañculā bowed deeply to her and, with joined palms and bowed head, questioned her with great affection. ॥10॥
m.5.11: Cañculā said: Where is my husband now? I do not know his condition at all. O sinless Girijā, so that I may be united with him— ॥11॥
m.5.12: —do just that, O auspicious one, out of compassion, O you who love the afflicted. O great goddess, O Maheśānī, my husband was the lover of a low-caste woman; the sinner died before me, and I do not know what destination he has gone to. ॥12॥
m.5.13: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Cañculā, Pārvatī Girijā, who loves right conduct, replied with great affection. ॥13॥
m.5.14: Girijā said: Listen: your husband, named Binduga, a great sinner of wicked intent, an enjoyer of prostitutes, a great fool—having died, he went to hell. ॥14॥
m.5.15: Having suffered the various torments of hell for countless years, that sinful soul, by the remainder of his sin, was born in the Vindhya as a piśāca. ॥15॥
m.5.16: Now he is a piśāca, beset with many afflictions; right there, wicked, living on air, he constantly bears every hardship. ॥16॥
m.5.17: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Gaurī, that Cañculā of auspicious vows then became distressed with great grief over her husband, it is said. ॥17॥
m.5.18: Then, composing her mind and bowing deeply to the great goddess, that woman, with a tormented heart, asked again. ॥18॥
m.5.19: Cañculā said: O Maheśvarī, O great goddess, show compassion to me. Rescue today my husband, that villain, the doer of wicked deeds. ॥19॥
m.5.20: By what means might my husband, that sinful, evil-minded one, attain a good destination, O goddess? Tell that quickly; salutations to you. ॥20॥
m.5.21: Sūta said: Hearing her words, Pārvatī, affectionate to devotees, with a gracious mind, replied to Cañculā, her own friend. ॥21॥
m.5.22: Pārvatī said: If your husband were to hear the holy, supreme story of Śiva, he would cross over all misfortune and attain a good destination. ॥22॥
m.5.23: Having heard these nectar-syllabled words of Gaurī, she then, with reverence, palms joined and shoulders bowed, prostrated again and again. ॥23॥
m.5.24: Then she begged her for her husband's hearing of that story, for the purification of all his sins and for his attainment of a good destination. ॥24॥
m.5.25: Sūta said: Being entreated again and again by that woman, Gaurī, beloved of Śiva, the great goddess affectionate to devotees, became filled with compassion. ॥25॥
m.5.26: Then the mountain's daughter, having summoned with affection Tumburu, king of the Gandharvas, singer of Śiva's true glory, said this: ॥26॥
m.5.27: Girijā said: O Tumburu, dear to Śiva, fulfiller of my wishes, go quickly with this woman to the Vindhya mountain—blessings to you. ॥27॥
m.5.28: There dwells a most dreadful, terrifying piśāca. Hear his history with goodwill; I shall tell you all of it from the beginning. ॥28॥
m.5.29: In his former birth that piśāca was a brahmin named Binduga, the wicked husband of this woman, my friend, and the lover of a low-caste woman. ॥29॥
m.5.30: He was devoid of bathing, twilight worship and rites, impure, his mind deluded by anger; an eater of bad food, a hater of good people, an acceptor of improper gifts. ॥30॥
m.5.31: He was violent and bore weapons, ate with his left hand, oppressed the poor, was cruel, and set fire to others' houses. ॥31॥
m.5.32: He was ever devoted to caṇḍāla women, an enjoyer of prostitutes, a great villain, a sinner who abandoned his own wife, delighting then in wicked company. ॥32॥
m.5.33: Through that evil association with a prostitute, his great merit was destroyed; out of greed for wealth, he made his wife a fearless adulteress. ॥33॥
m.5.34: That man of evil conduct, remaining so until death, in time met his end, and went to the dreadful city of Yama, the place where sinners undergo their fruits. ॥34॥
m.5.35: Having undergone many hells there, that wicked soul is now a piśāca on the Vindhya mountain, a villain reaping his sins. ॥35॥
m.5.36: Before him, narrate with care the supreme, holy, divine story of the Śiva Purāṇa, which destroys all sins. ॥36॥
m.5.37: Quickly, through hearing the supreme story of the Śiva Purāṇa, his soul purified of all sins, he will cast off his ghostly state. ॥37॥
m.5.38: And when that piśāca Binduga is freed from his evil state, you, by my command, bring him in an aerial chariot to Śiva's presence. ॥38॥
m.5.39: Sūta said: Thus commanded by Maheśānī, Tumburu, lord of the Gandharvas, rejoiced greatly in his mind and extolled his own good fortune. ॥39॥
m.5.40: Mounting a fine aerial chariot together with that virtuous woman, the beloved of that Binduga, he—dear to Nārada—went swiftly to the Vindhya mountain, where the piśāca dwelt. ॥40॥
m.5.41: There he saw that piśāca (goblin-ghost), huge-bodied and with a massive jaw, laughing, weeping and leaping about, of hideous form. ॥41॥
m.5.42: And Tumburu, the very mighty singer of Śiva's true glory, forcibly seized that extremely terrifying piśāca with nooses. ॥42॥
m.5.43: Then that Tumburu, having resolved upon the recitation of the Śiva Purāṇa, made arrangements accompanied by a great festival. ॥43॥
m.5.44: Tumburu has gone, at the Goddess's command, to liberate the piśāca, to make him hear the supreme Śiva Purāṇa on the Vindhya mountain. ॥44॥
m.5.45: Thus a great clamour arose in all the worlds, and the gods and sages hastened there to hear it. ॥45॥
m.5.46: There arose a supreme, wondrous and auspicious assembly of those who had come out of reverence to hear the Śiva Purāṇa. ॥46॥
m.5.47: Then, having bound that piśāca with nooses and seated him, Tumburu, lute in hand, sang the story of Gaurī's lord. ॥47॥
m.5.48: Beginning with the first saṃhitā up to the seventh saṃhitā, he clearly expounded the Śiva Purāṇa together with its māhātmya. ॥48॥
m.5.49: Having heard with reverence the Śiva Purāṇa of seven saṃhitās, all those listeners indeed became fulfilled through merit. ॥49॥
m.5.50: That piśāca, having heard the most meritorious Śiva Purāṇa, shook off all his sin and abandoned his ghostly body. ॥50॥
m.5.51: Swiftly he became divine in form, fair-complexioned, clad in white garments, his limbs shining with all ornaments, three-eyed and moon-crested. ॥51॥
m.5.52: Having become divine, of divine body, together with his own beloved wife, the glorious one himself also sang the deeds of Pārvatī's lord. ॥52॥
m.5.53: Seeing him and his wife thus, all those gods and sages became astonished in mind, filled with supreme bliss. ॥53॥
m.5.54: Fulfilled after hearing the wondrous deeds of Maheśa, they went joyfully each to his own abode, praising Śaṅkara's glory. ॥54॥
m.5.55: Binduga too, now divine in nature, seated in a fine celestial chariot, happy and glorious, at the side of his beloved, shone exceedingly, stationed in the sky. ॥55॥
m.5.56: Then, singing the most charming virtues of Maheśa, he with Tumburu and with his wife swiftly went to Śaṅkara's abode. ॥56॥
m.5.57: That Binduga was well honoured by Maheśa and Pārvatī, and was lovingly made one of his own gaṇas; she became a companion of Girijā. ॥57॥
m.5.58: In that world of supreme bliss, of dense light, eternal, having obtained an unshakable dwelling, the two enjoy supreme happiness. ॥58॥
m.5.59: Thus has been narrated this holy, sin-destroying legend, which brings the supreme bliss of Śiva and Śivā, is pure, and increases devotion. ॥59॥
m.5.60: Whoever hears this with devotion, or recites it with a concentrated mind, having enjoyed abundant pleasures, will attain liberation in the end. ॥60॥
m.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The attainment of a good end by Binduga, in the Śivapurāṇa Māhātmya of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
m.6.1: Śaunaka said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most wise one, disciple of Vyāsa, salutations to you. You are blessed; you are the foremost of Śaivas, whose great virtues deserve to be described. ॥1॥
m.6.2: Tell me the procedure for hearing the glorious Śiva Purāṇa, by which the listener may obtain everything — the complete and supreme fruit. ॥2॥
m.6.3: Sūta said: Now, O Śaunaka, O sage, I shall fully explain to you the procedure for hearing the Śiva Purāṇa, for the sake of obtaining the complete fruit. ॥3॥
m.6.4: Having summoned an astrologer and satisfied him, the sponsor, together with his people, should determine a pure auspicious time so that the recitation may be completed without obstacle. ॥4॥
m.6.5: That auspicious message should be sent with effort to every region: A Śaiva narration will take place; those who seek welfare should come. ॥5॥
m.6.6: Some are far from the stories of Hari, some far from the glorification of Śaṅkara; women, śūdras and others — let the message go out so that they may gain understanding. ॥6॥
m.6.7: The devotees of Śambhu in every region who are eager to hear the glorification should be respectfully brought, for the purpose of that event. ॥7॥
m.6.8: The invitation should say: Here there will be a gathering of the virtuous, a supreme festival, most wondrous, at the complete recitation of the Śaiva Purāṇa. ॥8॥
m.6.9: To drink the nectar called the glorious Śiva Purāṇa, may you kindly come quickly and respectfully, full of love. ॥9॥
m.6.10: If there is no leisure, you should lovingly come for a single day; coming is to be done by all means, for even a moment's stay here is hard to obtain. ॥10॥
m.6.11: In this way they should be invited humbly and joyfully; and when they have arrived, they should be honoured in every way. ॥11॥
m.6.12: An excellent place for hearing the Śiva Purāṇa should be prepared in a Śiva temple, at a sacred ford, in a forest, or else in a house. ॥12॥
m.6.13: The ground should be cleansed, plastered, and adorned with mineral colours; a varied, splendid decoration should be made, in the manner of a great festival. ॥13॥
m.6.14: Removing all the household articles that are unsuitable there, one should carefully place them out of sight in a secluded corner of the house. ॥14॥
m.6.15: A very lofty pavilion should be built, adorned with plantain-stem pillars, well decorated with fruits, flowers and the like, and resplendent with a canopy on all sides. ॥15॥
m.6.16: In the four directions flags should be raised, with banners, very beautiful; and sincere devotion, which brings joy to all, should be practised in every way. ॥16॥
m.6.17: A divine seat should be arranged for Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self; and likewise a fine seat, conducive to comfort, for the speaker. ॥17॥
m.6.18: Good places should be arranged for the listeners according to their rank, and ordinary places for the others, O sage. ॥18॥
m.6.19: Whatever joyful state of mind one has at a wedding, just such should be adopted here; all other worldly worries must be put away, O Śaunaka. ॥19॥
m.6.20: The speaker should face north and the listener east; the reverse arrangement of the two may also be understood — there is no conflict. ॥20॥
m.6.21: Or the east is to be reckoned according to the relation between the worshipped and the worshipper; or else the listeners' faces are prescribed to be turned towards the speaker. ॥21॥
m.6.22: When the twice-born Purāṇa-reciter has taken the seat of Vyāsa, he should not bow to anyone until the topic is completed. ॥22॥
m.6.23: Whether a boy, a youth or an old man, poor or weak, the knower of the Purāṇa is always to be saluted and honoured by those who seek merit. ॥23॥
m.6.24: One should never think lowly of a knower of the Purāṇa, whose speech issuing from his mouth is a wish-fulfilling cow for embodied beings. ॥24॥
m.6.25: There are indeed many gurus, by birth and by virtue; among them the knower of the Purāṇa is especially the supreme guru. ॥25॥
m.6.26: He who grants supreme liberation to those who suffer, being born again and again through thousands of crores of births — what other guru is higher than he? ॥26॥
m.6.27: One who knows the Purāṇa, who is pure, skilful, calm, free of envy, virtuous, compassionate and eloquent, should narrate this sacred story. ॥27॥
m.6.28: Beginning from sunrise and ending after three and a half watches, the story of the Śiva Purāṇa should be properly recited by the wise speaker. ॥28॥
m.6.29: Those who are rogues, those of evil conduct, and others who are bent on contention — before such crooked people one should never narrate the story. ॥29॥
m.6.30: One should not narrate this sacred story in a place crowded with wicked people, nor in one beset by robbers, nor in the house of a rogue. ॥30॥
m.6.31: At midday a pause in the recitation of the story should be made by the people for one muhūrta, for the purpose of passing stool and urine. ॥31॥
m.6.32: The speaker should get himself shaved a day before the start, in order to observe the vow; and all daily rites should be performed diligently but in brief. ॥32॥
m.6.33: Beside the speaker, another person of similar kind should be placed as an assistant — a learned man who dispels doubts and is intent on enlightening people. ॥33॥
m.6.34: To remove obstacles to the narration, one should worship Gaṇanātha, and with devotion Śiva, the lord of the story, and especially the book. ॥34॥
m.6.35: The wise listener, purified according to proper procedure, pure in heart and serene in mind, should hear the story of the Śiva Purāṇa with reverence. ॥35॥
m.6.36: A speaker or listener who is distracted by many activities, possessed of the six vices beginning with lust, attached to women, and a speaker of heretical doctrines, does not gain merit. ॥36॥
m.6.37: Casting aside worldly worries and anxieties about wealth, home and sons, he whose mind is on the story and whose intellect is pure obtains the supreme fruit. ॥37॥
m.6.38: Listeners endowed with faith and devotion, without longing for other affairs, restrained in speech, pure and undistracted, partake of merit. ॥38॥
m.6.39: Those vilest of men who hear this sacred story without devotion obtain no fruit from hearing; they have sorrow birth after birth. ॥39॥
m.6.40: Those fools who hear this story without having worshipped the Purāṇa with offerings according to their means become poor and are not purified. ॥40॥
m.6.41: Those men who go elsewhere while the story is being narrated: their possessions, such as wife and the rest, perish in the midst of their enjoyment. ॥41॥
m.6.42: And those men who listen to this story with turbans on their heads: their sons are born sinful, defilers of the family. ॥42॥
m.6.43: Those men who listen to this story while chewing betel: Yama's servants make them eat their own excrement in hell. ॥43॥
m.6.44: And those men who listen to this story seated on a high seat, having undergone all the hells, then indeed become crows. ॥44॥
m.6.45: Those who listen to this auspicious story seated in the vīra-posture and the like, having undergone all the hells, surely become poisonous trees. ॥45॥
m.6.46: Those men who listen to the story without bowing to the narrator, having undergone all the hells, become arjuna trees. ॥46॥
m.6.47: Those men who, though not sick, listen to this story lying down, having undergone all the hells, become pythons and the like. ॥47॥
m.6.48: Those who listen to this story seated on a seat equal to the narrator's: by such hell-bound ones a sin equal to violating the teacher's bed is always incurred. ॥48॥
m.6.49: And those who revile the narrator and this most purifying story become dogs, indeed, having suffered misery for a hundred births. ॥49॥
m.6.50: Those who speak ill words while the story is going on, having undergone dreadful hells, then become donkeys. ॥50॥
m.6.51: Those who never even listen to this most purifying story, having undergone dreadful hells, become wild boars. ॥51॥
m.6.52: Those wicked ones who cause obstruction while the story is being recited, having undergone hells for ten million years, become village pigs. ॥52॥
m.6.53: Having reflected thus, the wise listener, pure in mind and full of devotion toward the narrator, should be eagerly ready, with love, for the purpose of hearing the story. ॥53॥
m.6.54: To destroy obstacles to the story, he should first worship Gaṇeśa; having completed the daily rites, he should briefly perform an expiatory rite. ॥54॥
m.6.55: Having worshipped the nine planets and the deities of the sarvatobhadra diagram, he should worship that book according to the procedure prescribed for Śiva's worship. ॥55॥
m.6.56: At the end of the worship, with great devotion, joining his palms, humble, he should offer praise to the book, which is Śiva's very form. ॥56॥
m.6.57: You, named the glorious Śiva Purāṇa, are Maheśvara in visible form. You have been accepted by me for hearing; be pleased with me. ॥57॥
m.6.58: This wish of mine should be made fruitful by you; may my hearing of the story be fully completed without obstacle. ॥58॥
m.6.59: Lift me, wretched and sunk in the sea of worldly existence, out of the ocean of existence, my limbs seized by the crocodile of karma. I am your servant, O Śaṅkara. ॥59॥
m.6.60: Having thus praised the Śiva Purāṇa, which is Śiva's very form, and having spoken humble words, he should begin the worship of the narrator. ॥60॥
m.6.61: He should honour the narrator too by the procedure prescribed for Śiva's worship; he should worship him with flowers, garments and ornaments, and with incense, lamps and the like. ॥61॥
m.6.62: Then, in his presence, a vow should be taken with a pure mind, and it should be kept carefully, as far as one is able, until the completion. ॥62॥
m.6.63: O you who are in the form of Vyāsa, foremost in awakening others, expert in Śiva's scriptures, destroy my ignorance by the illumination of this story. ॥63॥
m.6.64: With devotion, five brahmins, or one, should be engaged, and they should constantly perform japa of Śiva's five-syllabled mantra. ॥64॥
m.6.65: Thus, O sage, I have told you with devotion the proper procedure for hearing the story, for listeners and devotees alike. What else do you wish to hear? ॥65॥
m.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The procedure for hearing, in the Śivapurāṇa Māhātmya of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
m.7.1: Śaunaka said: O Sūta, O Sūta, greatly wise one, foremost of Śaivas, you are blessed! You have made us hear this wondrous story, which brings auspiciousness. ॥1॥
m.7.2: O sage, out of compassion and for the welfare of all the worlds, tell us the rules for men who take the vow of hearing the Śiva Purāṇa. ॥2॥
m.7.3: Sūta said: Listen with true devotion, Śaunaka, to the rules for those men. By hearing the holy story according to the rules, one gains the highest fruit, free of obstacles. ॥3॥
m.7.4: Men without initiation have no entitlement to hear the story. Therefore, O sage, those who wish to hear should receive initiation from the speaker. ॥4॥
m.7.5: The one under the vow of the story should always observe celibacy, sleep on the ground, eat from a leaf-plate, and take his meal only when the day's recitation is finished. ॥5॥
m.7.6: One who is very strong should fast until the Purāṇa is completed and, pure, listen with devotion to the excellent Śaiva Purāṇa. ॥6॥
m.7.7: Or he may listen comfortably while taking ghee or milk; or it may be heard while living on fruit, or else on a single meal a day. ॥7॥
m.7.8: The one under the vow of this story should eat sacrificial food (haviṣya) once a day; the hearing should be done in whatever way it can be accomplished with ease. ॥8॥
m.7.9: I consider eating to be easy and conducive to hearing in the story-sessions; fasting is not better if it would obstruct the hearing of the story. ॥9॥
m.7.10: He should not listen after having eaten heavy food, split pulses, burnt food, niṣpāva beans, lentils, food tainted in intention, or stale food — so should the vow-keeper always observe. ॥10॥
m.7.11: Nor should the vow-keeper listen after eating brinjal, watermelon, snake-gourd, radish, pumpkin, coconut, or roots. ॥11॥
m.7.12: He who keeps the vow of the story should avoid onion, garlic, asafoetida, gṛñjana (a kind of onion), whatever is intoxicating, and things classed as flesh. ॥12॥
m.7.13: He who keeps the vow of the story should avoid the six passions beginning with desire, reviling of the twice-born, and slander of chaste wives and of the virtuous. ॥13॥
m.7.14: He who keeps the vow of the story should not look at a menstruating woman, should not narrate the story to the fallen, and should not speak with those hostile to the twice-born or outside the Veda. ॥14॥
m.7.15: The one under the vow of the story should always practise truthfulness, purity, compassion, silence, straightforwardness, humility, and generosity of mind. ॥15॥
m.7.16: Both the desireless and one with desires should hear the story according to the rules. One with desires obtains his desire; the desireless would attain liberation. ॥16॥
m.7.17: A poor man, one wasting with consumption, a sick man, a sinner, an unfortunate one, and even a man without offspring should hear this holy story. ॥17॥
m.7.18: The seven kinds of unfortunate women, beginning with the kākavandhyā (one who bears only a single child), and the woman who suffers miscarriages — by both these the supreme story should be heard. ॥18॥
m.7.19: O sage, all — women and men alike — should diligently hear the story of this Śiva Purāṇa according to the rules. ॥19॥
m.7.20: The days of the complete recitation of this Śiva Purāṇa should be understood as most excellent and equal to ten million sacrifices. ॥20॥
m.7.21: Whatever thing, however small, is given according to rule on these most excellent days, one obtains imperishable fruit from it. ॥21॥
m.7.22: Having thus performed the procedure of the vow and heard this supreme story, the fortunate one, filled with the highest bliss, should then perform the concluding rite (udyāpana). ॥22॥
m.7.23: The procedure of this concluding rite is held to be the same as that of the Caturdaśī vow; the wealthy who desire the fruit declared for it should perform it in the same way. ॥23॥
m.7.24: For devotees who possess nothing, there is generally no insistence on the concluding rite; they are purified by the hearing alone and are regarded as desireless followers of Śambhu. ॥24॥
m.7.25: Thus, when the festival-sacrifice of the complete recitation of the Śiva Purāṇa is finished, worship should be performed with devotion and care by the listeners. ॥25॥
m.7.26: O sage, first worship of the book should be duly performed, properly, just like the worship of Śiva, and after that worship of the speaker. ॥26॥
m.7.27: For wrapping the book one should offer a new, auspicious cloth-seat, and for binding it a strong, fine cord. ॥27॥
m.7.28: Those who give cord and new cloth for the Purāṇa become enjoyers of prosperity and endowed with knowledge in birth after birth. ॥28॥
m.7.29: To the speaker one should give various precious things — clothes, ornaments, and vessels — splendid and abundant, especially. ॥29॥
m.7.30: Those men who give, for the seat of the Purāṇa, blankets, deerskins, cloths, a stand, or a board — ॥30॥
m.7.31: — having reached the heavenly world and enjoyed pleasures as they wish, and having stayed in Brahmā's realm for a kalpa, they then go to Śiva's abode. ॥31॥
m.7.32: Having thus performed, according to procedure, the worship of the book and of the speaker, O tiger among sages, with a great festival, ॥32॥
m.7.33: one should accordingly worship the scholar appointed to assist, with wealth and the like somewhat less than for the speaker. ॥33॥
m.7.34: To the brāhmaṇas who have assembled one should give food, wealth, and so on; a great festival should be held with songs, instrumental music, and dances. ॥34॥
m.7.35: If the listener is a renunciant, then on the following day especially, O sage, the Gītā spoken by Śiva to Rāmacandra should be recited. ॥35॥
m.7.36: If the listener is a householder, that wise man should perform a fire-offering (homa) with pure oblation, for the pacification of any faults of that rite. ॥36॥
m.7.37: The homa should be done with the Rudra Saṃhitā, verse by verse, O sage, or with the Gāyatrī, since this Purāṇa is in essence made of it. ॥37॥
m.7.38: Or it may be done with Śiva's root mantra of five syllables. If unable to perform the homa, the wise man should give the oblation-material meant for the homa to a brāhmaṇa. ॥38॥
m.7.39: And to remove the two faults called deficiency and excess, one should recite or listen with devotion to the Thousand Names of Śiva. ॥39॥
m.7.40: By that everything becomes fruitful — fruitful, there is no doubt here — for there is nothing in the three worlds greater than this. ॥40॥
m.7.41: He should feed eleven brahmins with honey and milk-rice, and give them a fee (dakṣiṇā) so that the vow is fully accomplished. ॥41॥
m.7.42: If he is able, O sage, he should have a beautiful lion-throne made with gold weighing three palas, and on it place this Purāṇa in auspicious letters, ॥42॥
m.7.43: a copy either written by another or written by himself, the man, having duly installed it and worshipped it with the services beginning with invocation, along with a fee, ॥43॥
m.7.44: the wise man should give it to the self-controlled teacher, who has been honoured with garments, ornaments, perfumes and the like, for the sake of pleasing Śiva. ॥44॥
m.7.45: By the power of that gift of this Purāṇa, O Śaunaka, having obtained Śiva's grace, he becomes freed from the bondage of worldly existence. ॥45॥
m.7.46: When the rite is performed in this way, the glorious Śiva Purāṇa truly yields its full fruit and bestows both enjoyment and liberation. ॥46॥
m.7.47: Thus I have told you everything: the greatness of the glorious Śiva Purāṇa, which grants all desires. What more do you wish to hear? ॥47॥
m.7.48: The glorious Śiva Purāṇa is regarded as the crown-mark among Purāṇas; it is great, dear to Śiva, delightful, and removes the disease of worldly existence. ॥48॥
m.7.49: They truly have gained the fruit of birth in the world of the living who always meditate on Viśvanātha, whose speech praises his qualities, and whose two ears hear his story; they cross over worldly existence. ॥49॥
m.7.50: I take refuge in the Supreme Śiva, whose form is ever unmanifest through all the distinctions of qualities, who by his majesty shines outside and within in the world, who in the mind, outside and within, has the form of the activities of speech and mind, and who is dense with infinite bliss. ॥50॥
m.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The rules and prohibitions for those keeping the vow of hearing the Śrī Śivapurāṇa, and the worship of the book and the speaker, in the Sanatkumāra-saṃhitā of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
